metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Thermal Physics — Definition of Specific Heat Capacity
metadata.note: 3m: define specific heat capacity. 3-slot cloze: energy/heat(0.5m) + 1 kg of substance(1.5m) + 1°C or 1K(1m). Key discriminator: must specify BOTH '1 kg' AND '1°C'. Missing either drops the mark.

question.name: CSEC Phy Jun 2023 Q1a — Define Specific Heat Capacity
question.text:
Define the term 'specific heat capacity' by completing the statement below:

The specific heat capacity of a substance is the amount of [[1]] required to raise the temperature of [[2]] of the substance by [[3]].
question.general_feedback:
Specific heat capacity (c):

The specific heat capacity of a substance is the amount of thermal energy (heat) required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of the substance by 1 °C (or 1 K).

Formula: Q = mcΔθ → c = Q/(mΔθ)

SI unit: J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹ or J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹

Example: Water has c = 4200 J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹ — it takes 4200 J to heat 1 kg of water by 1 °C. This high value explains why oceans moderate climate.

ddwtos.cloze_html: The specific heat capacity of a substance is the amount of [[1]] required to raise the temperature of [[2]] of the substance by [[3]].

groups.label: SHC — amount of ___ required
groups.diagnostic_hint: Specific heat capacity is the amount of THERMAL ENERGY (heat energy) required. "Energy" alone is accepted at CSEC level.

groups.label: SHC — energy to raise the temperature of ___ of substance
groups.diagnostic_hint: The "specific" in SHC means PER UNIT MASS, specifically 1 kg. If you had 2 kg, you would need twice as much energy.

groups.label: SHC — energy to raise temperature by ___
groups.diagnostic_hint: SHC is defined for a temperature rise of 1°C (or equivalently 1 K — the same size interval). Q = mcΔT, so c = Q/(mΔT).

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 13 tokens for 3 slots. Slot 1 (energy type): thermal energy/heat energy/energy all accepted — these are synonymous in this context. 'Power' is wrong (energy per unit time, W). 'Work done' is technically energy but implies a mechanical context. Slot 2 (1 kg): '1 gram' is wrong — the specific heat capacity uses 1 kg (SI base unit). Some textbooks define molar heat capacity (1 mole) but CSEC uses the 1 kg definition. 'Any mass' is wrong — the definition requires a specific standard mass. Slot 3 (1°C / 1K): both accepted — a change of 1°C equals a change of 1K. '1°F' uses Fahrenheit (non-SI). '100°C' is wrong — that is the temperature change for an entirely different concept.
